chains.trait: Dense vascular fur patches on lumbar region
links: High O2 partial pressure (F7) drives rapid host metabolism
Saturated humidity (F8) traps convective heat near the body
Parasite attachment sites require stable thermoregulation
Vascular fur acts as a biological heat-sink and saddle

skill.effect: Share 15% stamina with paired parasite over 3 turns

chains.weakness: Fur mats absorb moisture, slowing movement in dry seasons

journal.en: Evolution built a living saddle long before they invented the stirrup.

plausibility.summary: Treat as short, sparse pelage over a brood-patch–like vascularized dermis (radiator, not insulator); note year-round high RH (F8) raises dermatophyte risk unless sebaceous/antimicrobial coevolution with the rider is stated.
fixes: Treat as short, sparse pelage over a brood-patch–like vascularized dermis (radiator, not insulator); note year-round high RH (F8) raises dermatophyte risk unless sebaceous/antimicrobial coevolution with the rider is stated.

analogues.organism: Brood-patch vasculature in incubating birds; elephant/caribou ear countercurrent thermoregulation; oxpecker–ungulate contact zones on thin, perfused skin
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Enlarged nasal turbinates for chemical steering
links: Dense humid air (F8) preserves volatile scent plumes
High pressure (F6) extends odor travel distance
Parasite navigation replaces host motor control
Enlarged turbinates track chemical leashes for pathfinding

skill.effect: leads host or ally 50m along chemical path

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to strong olfactory masking agents; loses navigation

journal.en: Their sense of smell is a leash they never learned to break.

plausibility.summary: Pair enlarged turbinates with enlarged olfactory bulbs and lore-accurate parasite steering via touch/olfaction (F17); in 85% RH some volatiles are less airborne—use both polar (dissolved) and volatile trails, not long-range monomolecular plumes alone.
fixes: Pair enlarged turbinates with enlarged olfactory bulbs and lore-accurate parasite steering via touch/olfaction (F17); in 85% RH some volatiles are less airborne—use both polar (dissolved) and volatile trails, not long-range monomolecular plumes alone.

analogues.organism: Canid enlarged ethmoturbinates; rat spatial map via sniffing; parasitic manipulation of host behavior (e.g., rabies/Drosophila parasitoid analogues for steering metaphor only)
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Hosts develop vascular fur and chemical steering to manage infestation; parasites refine abdominal suckers and pain-soothing saliva into mutualistic neural puppetry.
Symbiotes trade cognitive enhancement for host mobility; hosts gain protection and efficient resource gathering via tactile-olfactory interface.
